excerpt_original: Miami artists respond to GTA VI, Thelma Golden steps down from her role at the Studio Museum, and Hyperallergic has a brand new look.

blocks.text: As I walk by the Coptic Orthodox Church, I stumble upon damp, torn pages of an abandoned book on the sidewalk. The book is titled Existence: A New Dimension in Psychiatry and Psychology (1958), and the chapter I land on appears to be about ”ontological guilt.”

“If it is unaccepted and repressed, it may turn into neurotic guilt,” warns one line that weathered the elements. Across the street, a shop selling religious trinkets has a poster of a handsome, dark-haired Christ looking resolutely to the heavens in his crown of thorns.

In a bathroom on the 16th floor of the Bellevue Hotel in Philadelphia, I examine my pores in a 10x magnifying vanity mirror. I discover new unsettling facts about my face, but the extreme magnification also makes me appreciate the overlooked beauty in aging. Downstairs, the BlackStar Luminary Gala has already started. It’s a benefit dinner celebrating the 15th anniversary of the Philly-based nonprofit supporting Black, Brown, and Indigenous filmmakers and stories. I head down to the ballroom in my best clothes and find my seat at a table near the stage. “What are you doing here?” asks the first person I speak to.

On my way to the train station the next morning, I watch a cat almost get hit by a car as it attempts to cross a busy street outside the Masonic Temple. A woman with chalk-white skin glares at me with eyes so dark they look like someone has dug two deep wells in her face. Suddenly, the honey-sweet scent of a jasmine shrub emerges from the depths of my childhood memories.

Back in New York, I overhear two young men having a discussion about Thanksgiving. “Dude, it’s like celebrating the Nakba ,” one of them says, and then goes on to describe his complicated relationship with his old man. “He knows I give him a lot of grace,” he says about his father while a prematurely installed Christmas tree glints behind him.

I listen to Sally Rooney’s Normal People and then to Neil Young’s “Break the Chain.” The trees are skeletal and a big storm is about to come. Bored of the same old way home, I take a detour to explore an unknown street, and then quickly hit a dead end.
— Hakim Bishara, editor-in-chief
Hyperallergic has a new look!

From the start in 2009, Hyperallergic has been kicking at the doors of the art world status quo, challenging assumptions about what is worthy of investigation and investment, and the supposed neutrality of those decisions. Today, 17 years later, we are no longer a young upstart blogazine but a daily source of trusted news, reviews, and opinions for millions in the art community.
We are excited to introduce the next transformation of this site, with a whole new look, a dynamic homepage, and the third version of our wordmark. | Veken Gueyikian
